findings.finding: Timing difference between failure paths: for unknown users and locked accounts the Argon2 verification is skipped, so a failed login returns measurably faster than a wrong password. That reveals which usernames exist and which are locked, violating R1's intent. Always perform one verification (against a fixed dummy hash when there is no user) before deciding.
`locked` should default to false for existing serialized users; confirm #[serde(default)] is present (it is).

changes.description: Fixed Argon2id hash used to equalise timing when no user exists.

responses.explanation: PRIVATE-CODER-RESPONSE-91c2: Every path now runs exactly one Argon2 verification (against a cached dummy hash when the user is unknown) and only then checks `locked`, so unknown, locked and wrong-password failures cost the same.
PRIVATE-CODER-RESPONSE-0b55: #[serde(default)] is already on the field; no change needed.
